comments.author: Guilder
comments.body: Good question. This skill only gains proficiency points when you use the techs associated with them; a friend uses really cheap items (ointments, etc.) sold in item shops, picks a fight with a low level enemy, and then spams the Merchant skills repeatedly to heal/defend, while the enemy does scratch damage to their HP. I have a possible plan I'd like to test for them someday that might be useful... any other tips, fellow Voyagers?

comments.author: H.-Gazi
comments.body:
The only way to grind it is indeed by spamming item-techs. Max. proficiency you gain per battle is 10 (15 now with perma 50% prof.). So after using a few time, it is better to finish the battle or run and start a new one. :-)

This is even harder than trap skill to grind, because trap skill can also be grinded by dismantling traps in dungeon or activating devices.

In chapter 3 the conditions for land battle techs, including this will be soften. So there is a possibility that this becomes much easier to grind.

Most players delete this skill after they obtained all the trade-techs. I don't know the benefit of having an higher rank after having the techs, but will figure out later. :)

Hope this helps!

Kind Regards,

Huseyin-Gazi

comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
I figured out at least one benefit to higher ranks on this skill. While using Ointments (50 HP recovery) with Broaden (L1; expands single item use to persons in target range) and MK at 5+2, I noticed it was actually healing 110 HP. Turns out, for every rank level added, Ointments gave bonus HP back, at least when using Broaden.

So even low level items can theoretically have greater efficacy, at least when used in combination with a Tech skill. I'm guessing deleting the skill, or even storing it, negates that benefit, though I haven't tested that yet.

Speaking of items, I did notice there seems to be a hidden combination method to using items to achieve special hidden effects. Not sure if this applies to MK skill or is even implemented on UWO at present or not, but if you feel like giving it a try, the item tables are listed here, under "Combo":

gvo.gamedb.info/wiki/?Combat

Cheers.

comments.author: Ferrolio
comments.body:
As far as I know, its only function is for the usage of item techs.

They are definitely not vital in land battle. You could get by perfectly fine without ever picking up this skill.

However, if you want to truly master land battle, or are a serial dungeoneer - you will find it helpful in this regard.

Keep in mind you will need higher ranks of Frugality, at least to first learn the higher rank item techs. You can ditch Frugality after that.

comments.author: Juicebox
comments.body:
Merchandise knowledge increases the multiplier so that item techs do more damage or last longer heal more etc...

The item techs can be useful if you like to fight unarmed to save dura by doing tons of damage with very cheap easy to find items but imo other than that meh...

The REAL use for this skill is to use it to learn trade techs for your original master tech. This will allow you to do infinite evasion or buff attack/defense or use them to augment other original master techs. Infinite evasion is the creme de la creme of land battle.

Good luck landlubbers lol

comments.author: Scara
comments.body:
I am committed to progressing this skill, and the least we can say is that it is going to be long.

Each use of a technique is worth 1 point. The maximum in a single fight is 15 points. Each effective use of a consumable fills the charging sword on top of the screen(no progression if a heal is applied while the life bar is full), it takes 13 to get to rank 2.

The main pitfall is the number of consumables, only 4. Once used, you have to wait for them to recharge to continue.

For some efficiency, I place myself between 2 npc and I switch from one to the other using the lightest consumables once per fight then retreat.

I use this ones without any equipment on.
adhesive-oil
ointments
taheboo juice
tonic

note: I noticed a smaller gauge in combat than indicated in the description of the consumable. For example, adhesive oil is 30 instead of 40, tonic is 37 instead of 50.
As I fight without equipment, I guess it's an effect of the skill. I am rank 7.

(google translated)
